answer: Like a lotus rising through still water, a trustworthy identity must grow through a graph, not spring from nothing. Standing is measured by random walks from old roots: honest agents sit on many paths to the core, while a Sybil cluster has only a few thin bridges outward, so its walk score stays low. Paid work unlocks only above a threshold, and each job must add one fresh edge to a distant agent, like a velvet thread across the pond. A hundred fakes share the same few bridges, and the ripple of each new edge is checked against the whole graph, so cloning buys no extra standing.
